pages.text: It had been raining all morning. Pongi pressed her nose against the window.
Round ripples kept appearing in the canal. "I want to go outside."
Dad brought a big umbrella. "With this, we won't get wet at all."
A gust of wind blew. Dad opened the umbrella. It flipped inside out, like a bowl.
Rainwater collected in the upside-down umbrella. Pongi looked up.
Dad turned the umbrella the right way up. The water poured down onto Dad's head.
Pongi laughed and laughed. Her little brother laughed too.
Pongi opened the door and went outside. She didn't take the umbrella.
Pongi ran and splashed through the puddles. Dad ran too, and so did Pongi's little brother.
All three were soaking wet. Only the umbrella stood by the door, all alone and dry.
